The Black moray Muraena augusti is a large anguilliform species inhabiting rocky substrates and cave systems in the eastern Atlantic. Neonates of this species emerge from the egg at a very small size, with a wet weight at birth recorded at 0.536 grams [Wwb = 0.536 grams], a value consistent with the egg diameter of approximately 10 mm observed in the congeneric Muraena helena. Incubation under controlled laboratory conditions at a stable water temperature of 19.6 °C [T = 19.6 °C] resulted in an age at birth of 105 days [ab = 105 days], a duration that reflects the protracted developmental period typical of muraenid embryos. Upon hatching, the yolk-sac larva relies entirely on its endogenous yolk reserves before initiating first exogenous feeding. This lecithotrophic phase is critical for the initial growth of the prolarva, which must absorb its yolk mass fully before it can successfully capture prey. The timing of the hatching event is strongly influenced by thermal conditions, and the observed eclosion period at this temperature aligns well with records for the Mediterranean congener.

In assessing the species' maximal size, field surveys have identified an ultimate total length Li of 90 cm [Li = 90 cm] for fully grown adults. Corresponding to this length, the ultimate wet weight Wwi reaches 1667 grams [Wwi = 1667 grams], a mass derived from length-weight regressions that consolidate data across multiple capture events. These measurements place Muraena augusti as a moderately-sized moray, comparable to other members of the genus found in Macaronesian waters. The total length at which gonadal development is initiated, or the total length at puberty Lp, has been determined as 55.8 cm [Lp = 55.8 cm]. Individuals attaining this length are considered to have entered the sub-adult stage, having completed the allometric shifts associated with the larval-juvenile transition. At this length, the wet weight at puberty Wwp is estimated at 346 grams [Wwp = 346 grams], indicating that approximately one-fifth of the ultimate body mass is attained before reproductive maturation begins. These size thresholds are critical for understanding the species' life history and for informing fishery management.

Under the thermal regime typical of its range, maintained at 19.6 °C [T = 19.6 °C], the gonadosomatic index (GSI) is approximately 12.5% [GSI = approximately 12.5%]. This value, which is based on comparative data from Muraena helena, suggests a moderate reproductive effort relative to body size. Such an index is indicative of a strategy where energy is partitioned between somatic growth and gamete production across multiple spawning seasons. This allocation strategy is typical of iteroparous teleosts that undergo multiple reproductive events over their lifespan. Further histological analysis would help confirm whether the gonadal recrudescence pattern supports a protracted spawning season.

The lifespan of Muraena augusti in its natural environment is a crucial demographic parameter. Recent field studies and tag-recapture data, consolidated with observations on the congeneric Muraena helena, indicate a maximum lifespan of 38 years [am = 38 years] at 19.6 °C [T = 19.6 °C]. This longevity is relatively extended for a muraenid and suggests a slow life history pace characterized by delayed maturity and low natural mortality in the adult stage. The species' benthic, crevice-dwelling habit likely reduces predation risk, contributing to this long lifespan. Senescent adults may show decreased feeding efficiency and a gradual decline in body condition before eventually succumbing to physiological death. The survival of large, old individuals is ecologically important, as they may act as reservoirs of genetic diversity within the population. Future work should validate this lifespan estimate with direct otolith ageing across different geographic locations.

Comparisons between Muraena augusti and other anguilliforms highlight its relatively slow growth and delayed maturation schedule. The ultimate total length Li of 90 cm [Li = 90 cm] and the associated ultimate wet weight Wwi of 1667 grams [Wwi = 1667 grams] are attained only after many years of growth. Notably, the total length at puberty Lp of 55.8 cm [Lp = 55.8 cm] and the corresponding wet weight at puberty Wwp of 346 grams [Wwp = 346 grams] indicate that approximately 62% of the ultimate length is reached before sexual maturation begins. This pattern is consistent with the species' need to attain a sufficiently large body size to support the energetic demands of reproduction. The gonadosomatic index of approximately 12.5% [GSI = approximately 12.5%] was recorded at 19.6 °C [T = 19.6 °C]. The extended lifespan of 38 years [am = 38 years] at 19.6 °C [T = 19.6 °C] further positions this species as a K-selected strategist among teleosts.
